title: Counit-normalized ambient transpose and closure comparison-unit calculus
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal P,\mathcal Q$ be categories (with Hom sets and associative unital composition) [def-nagata-category]. Give functors $F_e:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $J_e:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $F_p:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$, $J_p:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal P$, $C_S:\mathcal A\to\mathcal P$, $C_T:\mathcal B\to\mathcal Q$ and adjunctions $F_e\dashv J_e$, $F_p\dashv J_p$, with counits $\epsilon^e,\epsilon^p$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Let $\mathcal A_0\subseteq\mathcal A$, $\mathcal B_0\subseteq\mathcal B$, $\mathcal Q_0\subseteq\mathcal Q$ be full subcategories with $C_T(\mathcal B_0)\subseteq\mathcal Q_0$; assume $F_e(\mathcal A_0)\subseteq\mathcal B_0$ and $C_T$ induces bijections on Hom sets between objects of $\mathcal B_0$. Give a functor $U:\mathcal Q_0\to\mathcal B$ and a natural transformation $\eta:1_{\mathcal B_0}\to UC_T|_{\mathcal B_0}$ (for instance the unit of an adjunction $C_T\dashv U$, restricted to $\mathcal B_0$); no adjunction $C_T\dashv U$ on all of $\mathcal B,\mathcal Q$ is assumed. Fix $M\in\mathcal B_0$ with $H=J_eM\in\mathcal A_0$ and invertible $\eta_M$. Give a natural isomorphism $\Delta:C_TF_e|_{\mathcal A_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_pC_S|_{\mathcal A_0}$ and an isomorphism $\gamma:C_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}J_pC_TM$ satisfying
$$\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma)\Delta_H=C_T(\epsilon^e_M).$$
Give functors $E_e:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $E_p:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ with $E_e(\mathcal A_0)\subseteq\mathcal B_0$ and natural isomorphisms $q_e:F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}E_e$, $q_p:F_p\xrightarrow{\sim}E_p$. Equip $E_e\dashv J_e$ with the adjunction transported along $q_e$, so its transpose sends $a:E_eL\to N$ to $\operatorname{adj}_e(aq_{e,L})$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Give a natural isomorphism $B:C_TE_e|_{\mathcal A_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_pC_S|_{\mathcal A_0}$ with $q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=B_LC_T(q_{e,L})$. For $z:E_pC_SL\to C_TM$ define
$$\Phi_{L,C_TM}(z)=C_S\!\left(\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv J_e}(U(zB_L)\eta_{E_eL})\right),\qquad \rho=C_SJ_e(\eta_M).$$
Then every $h:F_pC_SL\to C_TM$, $L\in\mathcal A_0$, has a unique lift $h_0:F_eL\to M$ with $h\Delta_L=C_T(h_0)$. With $g_0=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0)$, $z=hq_{p,C_SL}^{-1}$ and $a=h_0q_{e,L}^{-1}$ one has
$$zB_L=C_T(a),\quad \operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv J_e}(a)=g_0,\quad U(zB_L)\eta_{E_eL}=\eta_Ma,$$
$$\operatorname{adj}_p(h)=\gamma C_S(g_0),\qquad \Phi_{L,C_TM}(z)=\rho C_S(g_0).$$
The map $\rho:C_SH\to C_SJ_eUC_TM$ is invertible. These formulas are natural in $L$, and in any full subcategory of choices of $M$ for which the stated hypotheses hold and $\gamma$ is natural. Composition is read right to left. No full faithfulness outside $\mathcal B_0$ is assumed.

source.place: Second paragraph: locally closed exceptional comparison; returned expanded Steps 2–5 (unique lift, ambient counit, closure conjugation and comparison unit). Agent-formulated categorical consequence of Stacks categories.tex, Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint) and Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints).

proof.text: Both $F_eL$ and $M$ belong to $\mathcal B_0$. Apply the assumed bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(F_eL,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Q}(C_TF_eL,C_TM)$ to $h\Delta_L$. Its unique preimage is $h_0$, giving exactly $C_T(h_0)=h\Delta_L$. This uses full faithfulness only on these two objects.

proof.text: Put $g_0=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0):L\to H$. The inverse-transpose formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives $h_0=\epsilon^e_M F_e(g_0)$. Fullness of $\mathcal A_0$ makes $g_0$ a morphism of $\mathcal A_0$, since both $L$ and $H$ are in it; thus naturality of $\Delta$ applies to this morphism.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation for the locally closed comparison in the second paragraph of lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison.proof.md

proof.text:
Use the inverse-transpose formula for $F_p\dashv J_p$ on $\gamma C_S(g_0)$. After precomposing with $\Delta_L$, its value is
$$\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma)F_pC_S(g_0)\Delta_L
=\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma)\Delta_H C_TF_e(g_0)
=C_T(\epsilon^e_M)C_TF_e(g_0)
=C_T(h_0)=h\Delta_L.$$
The first equality is naturality of $\Delta$ at $g_0$ and the second is the assumed counit equation. Cancel the invertible $\Delta_L$; bijectivity of the adjunction transpose now gives $\operatorname{adj}_p(h)=\gamma C_S(g_0)$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation for the locally closed comparison in the second paragraph of lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison.proof.md

proof.text:
The compatibility of $B$ with $q_e,q_p$ implies
$$q_{p,C_SL}^{-1}B_L=\Delta_L C_T(q_{e,L}^{-1}).$$
Indeed multiply $q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=B_LC_T(q_{e,L})$ on the left by $q_{p,C_SL}^{-1}$ and on the right by $C_T(q_{e,L}^{-1})$. Hence, with the specified $z,a$,
$$zB_L=h\Delta_L C_T(q_{e,L}^{-1})=C_T(h_0q_{e,L}^{-1})=C_T(a).$$

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation for the locally closed comparison in the second paragraph of lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison.proof.md

proof.text:
By the transported-adjunction formula assumed in the statement,
$$\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv J_e}(a)=\operatorname{adj}_e(aq_{e,L})=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0)=g_0.$$
Here $a:E_eL\to M$ has both objects in $\mathcal B_0$. Naturality of the given $\eta$ at $a$, and the preceding equality $zB_L=C_T(a)$, give
$$U(zB_L)\eta_{E_eL}=UC_T(a)\eta_{E_eL}=\eta_Ma.$$
All applications of $U$ are to morphisms between objects of $\mathcal Q_0$, since it is full and contains $C_T(\mathcal B_0)$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation for the locally closed comparison in the second paragraph of lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison.proof.md

proof.text:
Apply right-variable naturality of the adjunction Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to $a:E_eL\to M$ followed by $\eta_M:M\to UC_TM$. It says
$$\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv J_e}(\eta_Ma)=J_e(\eta_M)\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv J_e}(a)=J_e(\eta_M)g_0.$$
The definition of $\Phi$ and Step 5 therefore give
$$\Phi_{L,C_TM}(z)=C_S(J_e(\eta_M)g_0)=\rho C_S(g_0).$$
No membership assumption on $UC_TM$ in $\mathcal B_0$ is needed: this adjunction is defined on all of $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation for the locally closed comparison in the second paragraph of lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison.proof.md

proof.text: Let $t:UC_TM\to M$ be the inverse of $\eta_M$. The morphism $C_SJ_e(t)$ is a two-sided inverse of $\rho=C_SJ_e(\eta_M)$: the two composites are $C_SJ_e(t\eta_M)=C_SJ_e(1_M)=1_{C_SH}$ and $C_SJ_e(\eta_Mt)=C_SJ_e(1_{UC_TM})=1_{C_SJ_eUC_TM}$. These equalities use functoriality and the identity and composition laws of [def-nagata-category].

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation for the locally closed comparison in the second paragraph of lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison.proof.md

proof.text: For $l:L'\to L$ in $\mathcal A_0$ put $h'=hF_pC_S(l)$. Naturality of $\Delta$ gives $h'\Delta_{L'}=h\Delta_L C_TF_e(l)=C_T(h_0F_e(l))$, so uniqueness of the lift gives $h'_0=h_0F_e(l)$. Left-variable naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives $g'_0=g_0l$. Naturality of $q_p$ and $q_e$ then gives $z'=zE_pC_S(l)$ and $a'=aE_e(l)$. Thus all three equalities of Step 5 precompose by the indicated maps. The two final transpose formulas precompose by $C_S(l)$, since $\gamma C_S(g'_0)=\gamma C_S(g_0)C_S(l)$ and $\rho C_S(g'_0)=\rho C_S(g_0)C_S(l)$. This proves naturality in $L$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation for the locally closed comparison in the second paragraph of lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison.proof.md

proof.text:
For $m:M\to M'$ between any two allowed choices, put $h'=C_T(m)h$. The lift is $h'_0=mh_0$, since $h'\Delta_L=C_T(mh_0)$; right-variable naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives $g'_0=J_e(m)g_0$. Also $z'=C_T(m)z$ and $a'=ma$. The assumed naturality of $\gamma$ gives $\gamma_{M'}C_SJ_e(m)=J_pC_T(m)\gamma_M$. Naturality of $\eta$ at $m$ gives
$$\rho_{M'}C_SJ_e(m)=C_SJ_e(\eta_{M'}m)=C_SJ_e(UC_T(m)\eta_M)=C_SJ_eUC_T(m)\rho_M.$$
Substitute these two equations and the formulas for $g'_0,z',a'$ into Steps 3–6. They show precisely that the ambient transpose is postcomposed by $J_pC_T(m)$, and $\Phi$ by $C_SJ_eUC_T(m)$; the three intermediate identities are postcomposed by $C_T(m)$, $J_e(m)$ and $UC_T(m)$ respectively. This proves the stated naturality in $M$, using only morphisms in the specified full subcategory.
